claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
The powder feedstock has a uniform nominal composition.
Build-platform preheating should be incorporated during laser powder bed fusion.
An optimized build-platform preheating temperature lies between 400°C and 600°C.
Build-platform preheating minimizes thermal gradients during additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Elevated substrate temperature moderately slows the cooling rate during rapid solidification.
Lower thermal gradients reduce residual thermal stress.
Lower thermal gradients and moderated cooling suppress compositional segregation.
Preheating produces a refined microstructure with reduced compositional gradients.
Reduced residual stress, segregation, and defects improve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
Preheated samples will have lower residual stress than samples fabricated without preheating.
Preheated samples will have less microsegregation and fewer defects than samples fabricated without preheating.
Preheated samples will exhibit higher tensile strength and ductility than samples fabricated without preheating.
Laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without substrate preheating is known to cause significant residual stress, microsegregation, and defect formation.
The outcome may depend on processing parameters and on a tradeoff between reduced segregation and microstructural coarsening.
The comparison should hold alloy composition, atmosphere, and other laser powder bed fusion conditions constant while varying substrate preheating.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in residual stress and microsegregation together with no measurable mechanical improvement would falsify the hypothesis.
